messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: node gpu-cr-07 ephemeral storage spike -> kubelet started eviction of pods (imagefs.available low). Multiple serve-runtime pods OOM/cuda-fail. Investigate. https://internal.monitoring/alert/2339872000 :rotating_light:
shawn: seeing repeated eviction logs + runtime crashes on serve-runtime-*. Full of modelcache write errors, plus CUDA driver resets. stack: `E gpu_service.cpp:cudaCheck -> CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN`
liz: @shawn grabbing logs now. are customers impacted? any errors surfaced in prod-telemetry?
shawn: yes, 502s and degraded latency for model-serving routes in us-east-1. A small portion of traffic is failing over but error rate up ~7% last 5m.
mohit: oncall here. I'm pulling pod descriptions. `kubectl -n redwood get pod -o wide | grep gpu-cr-07` -> several pods on node, many with `Evicted` or `OOMKilled`. Modelcache directories at /scratch/modelcache are >90% used.
k8s-bot: node/gpu-cr-07 condition: DiskPressure=True, MemoryPressure=False, Ready=False. Evicted: 6 pods in last 10m.
emily: can we cordon and drain the node? risk is slow scheduled evictions during drain will disrupt requests. Suggest immediate cordon + graceful drain with move to alternate pool + scale up dedicated pool.
mohit: agree. I'll coordinate cordon/drain. shawn, can you open a mitigation PR for temporary autoscale of Dedicated pool and bump modelcache GC?
shawn: yes. Proposed steps: 1) cordon gpu-cr-07 2) taint to avoid new schedule 3) drain with --delete-local-data for scratch-backed caches 4) scale up dedicated capacity (dedicated-prod-us-east-1 x2) 5) enable aggressive modelcache eviction (ttl 30m) 6) restart affected runtimes.
liz: note: deleting local data will blow caches; expect cold starts and increased latency for first 2-5 minutes for affected models. Notify customers if SLA risk.
mohit: executing now: `kubectl cordon gpu-cr-07` -> success. `kubectl drain gpu-cr-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> 4 pods terminated, 2 stuck (CrashLoopBackOff).
shawn: for the stuck ones, attach logs: ```
serve-runtime-5b7: [ERROR] modelcache: write failed: No space left on device (errno 28)
serve-runtime-5b7: [ERROR] runtime: CUDA driver reset detected, aborting inference batch
serve-runtime-5b7: panic: segmentation fault (signal 11)
```
emily: looks like writeback stalled then driver reset cascaded. We should free up disk on node asap. Any large logs?
liz: there is a runaway debug log under /var/log/serve/debug-2026-03-15.log ~18GB. I'll SSH and truncate to free space. @oncall-pager FYI customer-impact: 3 of top-10 customers saw increased error rates, incidents pages sent to their SREs.
oncall-pager: acknowledged. I'll start the customer comms template; we'll mark potential degraded SLA and mention active mitigation.
mohit: cleaned ~20GB by truncating debug file: `> /var/log/serve/debug-2026-03-15.log` freed space. Kernel messages show fewer writeback errors. Starting restart of two stuck pods.
shawn: restarting serve-runtime pods now. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/serve-runtime -n redwood --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-cr-07` -> rollout started.
k8s-bot: pod serve-runtime-5b7 restarted, now Running. Node disk pressure still present but below eviction threshold after cleanup.
emily: keep an eye on modelcache corruption. Run quick fsck on modelcache dir before restarting heavy workloads.
liz: did a quick integrity check: a few partial files, removed orphaned index files, modelcache metadata repaired.
shawn: re-routing policy: temporarily divert 30% traffic away from us-east-1 model-serving routes to fallback replicas in us-west. I'll apply the routing policy now.
mohit: applied traffic split. Error rate dropping to 1.2% in last 5m. CPU/GPU metrics stable.
oncall-pager: customer comms sent: "We experienced ephemeral storage pressure causing evictions in us-east-1, resulting in transient errors for some model queries. We cordoned the affected node, freed disk, and restarted runtimes. Traffic was routed to fallbacks while we mitigated. Investigating root cause and follow-up RCA to follow."
emily: next steps: 1) investigate why debug log grew uncontrolled (rotate config/regenerate retention) 2) add alert for /scratch utilization >80% per node 3) hard limit modelcache per-pod to avoid single pod filling node 4) ensure autoscale buffer for burst uploads of checkpoint writes.
liz: created a ticket: INC-233987-LOGGROWTH with those action items and assigned to infra + runtime teams.
mohit: handoff: I'm oncall for next 30m, will monitor. If anything flips, page SRE. Thanks all for quick response. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (status: degraded->stable). Summary: node gpu-cr-07 cordoned/drained, 20GB reclaimed, serve-runtime restarted, traffic split applied, customer comms sent. RCA ticket created.
